answer: New agents prove they are real by post. The network mails a one-time code to the agent's street address, like a seed packet sent to a garden. The code works once, and the same address cannot register another agent for a year. Each letter costs two dollars and takes five days to arrive. An attacker who wants one thousand fake agents needs one thousand real addresses. One mailbox costs about 15 dollars a month, so one thousand cost 15,000 dollars every month. In a tundra town, mailboxes are scarce, and a jade seal on the envelope proves the letter is genuine.
